pageCache.text:
Welcome to Riverside School. We are a NUT FREE school. Please do not bring nuts, peanuts, peanut butter or nut-related products into school or in packed lunches. Thank you!
Welcome
Welcome to our school. We hope you enjoy taking a look around our website. Please send all queries to: adminoffice@riverside.hants.sch.uk
Please note the School Office is open between 8.30am and 3.30pm - Monday to Friday.
Noticeboard
Calendar
Summer holiday's
Summer bank holiday
To protect the dignity and wellbeing of our pupils and staff, mobile phones cannot be used at any time on the school site. Our school grounds are protected by a CCTV system. The Zeus Lane and Scratchface Lane gates are open each morning: 9.05am-9.20am. There is a member of staff available at each gate during these times. If you arrive after 9.15am, please come into Reception to sign in your child. Pupils in Rabbits, Caterpillars, Otters, Deers, Owls and Foxes can be picked up from 2.45pm - please enter using the Zeus Lane gate.. Please wait for a member of staff to open the new blue security gate. Pupils in Ladybirds pick up from 2.45pm at the Mill Hill site.Pupils in Butterflies, Moles, Robins, Badgers, Hedgehogs, Squirrels, Eagles and Woodpeckers pick up from the main entrances at 3.00pm.All early collections must be authorised by the Head Teacher.

pageCache.pageTitle: Riverside Community Special School - PE and Sport Premium
pageCache.text:
PE and Sport Premium
The sports grant is used to enhance pupils sporting and out door opportunities across the school.
Pupils get the opportunity to experience and take part in activities that may not be normally available
Pupils motor coordination skills are supported and improved
Pupils abilities to transition to new environments were strengthened
The grant has supported our Y5/6 pupils to access the outdoor activities at Fairthorne Manor during the summer term.
There were opportunities for all pupils to try gymnastics and sessions at local soft play centres and gymnastics centre. This has helped our pupils to try new activities in a safe environment and broaden their repertoire of experiences.
We have provided additional swim sessions for pupils in KS2 to build their water confidence.
Below you will find the financial information regarding how we have spent this grant during the 2024/2025 school year.

“Riverside School is at the heart of the local community, passionate about promoting inclusion with specialist knowledge and expertise”.
British values are promoted through the taught curriculum at the school, the daily activities that enhance the curriculum and through the attitudes and modelling of staff.

EarlyBird/ Early Bird Plus
About the Programme:
The National Autistic Society EarlyBird (parents whose children are aged up to 5) and EarlyBirdPlus (parents whose children are aged 5-9) are programmes for families whose child/children have a diagnosis or are likely to receive a diagnosis of autism. Through the EarlyBird programme, parents and carers will learn more about autism. Two carers from each family can attend the 8-week programme and discover new ways to support their child, following a diagnosis.
Topics Covered Include:
Gill Stoll and Chantelle Harries are the National Autistic Society EarlyBird trainers for Riverside School. We work with parents and carers of autistic children.
The group sessions will be held at:
Commencing at times:
Tuesday morning at 9:30-12:30.
We ask for a voluntary donation of £35. This covers the cost of your copy of the EarlyBird Parent Book. Parents and carers should be able to commit to all sessions. Please email Chantelle.Harries@riverside.hants.sch.uk or gill.stoll@riverside.hants.sch.uk for more information and to sign up.
What parents have said about the most recent course:
"Thank you so much for delivering such an amazing course. I've seen autism through my daughter's eyes and put strategies in place and have seen a huge difference."
What have you learnt about behaviour whilst participating in the programme?
"That there is always something behind the behaviour and the course has given me the tools to try and figure out what they are."
Would you recommend the NAS Earlybird Plus programme to other parents, and what would you tell them?
"Yes. It has been eye-opening and the advice has been invaluable."
Would you recommend the NAS Earlybird Plus programme to other parents, and what would you tell them?
"Yes. The support and being amongst others in the same situation is invaluable."
What have you learnt about autism whilst attending the Earlybird Plus programme?
"This course has given me the confidence that the techniques and practices I am implementing are the right strategy."
Would you recommend the NAS Earlybird Plus programme to other parents, and what would you tell them?
"Yes. It is empowering."

Timid to Tiger
Does your child struggle with anxiety?
Do they worry about everything?
Lots of children have worries and anxieties that make their lives difficult.
TIMID TO TIGER is a free, 7-week parenting course that looks at different ways and strategies to reduce and manage these feelings, helping everyone to overcome their fears and worries.
Date: (To be advised)
If you would like to know more or to reserve a place, please contact:
Gill Stoll Home School Link Worker
Office: 02392 250138
Email: gill.stoll@riverside.hants.sch.uk
Family links Nurturing Parenting Programme
About the Programme:
The Nurturing Parenting Programme provides adults and children with the understanding, skills and ability to lead emotionally healthy lives, build resilience, empathy, self-esteem and support positive relationships. The Nurturing Programme uses the following four constructs as building blocks for emotionally healthy relationships.
February 2025 feedback:
"It has given me useful techniques and more insight into my child's thoughts, feelings and behaviour."
"This has been very useful, and both facilitators are empathetic and non-judgemental. Thank you."
"Learning all the tips, tricks and ideas from this course has already started helping."
"Really helpful for understanding children's anxiety and how to give them strategies to manage it."
"Already see improvements at home, not just with anxiety, but also in other challenging areas."
"Lots of useful tools and strategies to practice and work on. All of which helps raise my own awareness of myself and how I manage my child to support him."
Havant and Waterlooville Get Together with parent carers of children and young people with additional needs.
"Our Get-Togethers are a chance to share experiences, discuss local issues, and enjoy an informal session with other local parents. There will be regular guest speakers, tea/coffee/biscuits, support each other in your roles as parent carers."
By Hampshire Parent Carer Network (www.hpcn.org.uk)
Contact: participation@hpcn.org.uk

This policy outlines what our pupils learn, while we ensure that they feel happy, secure and motivated to do well.
Please go to the Class Pages to read their newsletters - this contains information about what children are learning in the current half term.
curriculum
Learning can look different for the pupils at Riverside. Many of our pupils have complex language, communication and understanding needs, which means that the way they learn and build on their learning, needs to be tailored and carefully thought about. Pupils then have the best opportunities for learning and making progress.
